claims.statement: Termind builds distinct macOS (`TFM`) and iOS/iPadOS (`TFI`) application targets, while shared framework modules do not import the application targets; the application targets own native UI and lifetime behavior.

On macOS, TermindApp is the composition root: it creates one SwiftData container, prepares persistence and Keychain-backed services, constructs sync/outbox/repository dependencies, and retains one AppModel in SwiftUI state; failure to open the local container terminates startup rather than substituting an empty store.

AppModel is app-wide desktop coordination state, while WindowModel owns state that may differ per window—including workspaces, selection, sidebar and search state—and registered windows receive shared services without transferring workspace ownership to the app model.
The macOS main `WindowGroup` creates a fresh `WindowModel` per scene but injects the same `AppModel` and SwiftData container; it also declares a separate externally-driven authentication window.

The desktop native window coordinator registers and unregisters each `WindowModel`, handles workspace transfer/new-window requests, preserves system-restored geometry, and closes the window model when its native `NSWindow` closes.

macOS termination asks the user before quitting with pending external edits, then performs idempotent app-wide cleanup that closes windows and cancels/stops runtime services; the AppKit delegate replies when cleanup finishes or after a three-second fallback.

`TermindIOSApp` creates one `MobileAppModel` startup result, selects testing or live dependencies from the XCTest environment, injects the shared model container into its `WindowGroup`, and presents an unavailable-data view when initialization fails.

`MobileAppDependencies` is the mobile composition seam: live assembly creates one logged `RemoteConnectionCoordinator` shared by workspace connection and metrics services, while testing assembly enables in-memory operation and injectable platform services.

MobileAppModel owns the mobile app-wide container, libraries, sync, assistant, metrics, transfer, forwarding, workspace registry, descriptor store, and synchronized connection-history model; production persists Termind.store under Application Support while in-memory/test modes omit production sync.

Each `MobileRootView` creates a scene-local `MobileSceneModel` for navigation and presentation, reports its phase to the shared app model, and publishes it as a focused scene value; its sidebar-adaptable tabs retain per-feature navigation stacks.

Mobile live workspaces are app-wide: openWorkspace reuses an existing instance or publishes a newly constructed workspace before connecting, allowing multiple scenes to select one live workspace without duplicate initial connections.

Mobile cold launch restores only saved workspace descriptors, not live sessions: it loads valid descriptors, starts with no workspaces, clears live activities, and opens/connects a descriptor only on demand; descriptors contain only workspace ID, Host ID, title, and connection kind, excluding runtime command/path state.

Mobile background behavior is aggregated across scenes: only when all tracked scenes are backgrounded does the app suspend sync/monitoring and begin a finite background task; expiry suspends workspace, forwarding, transfer, and assistant runtime work, while an active scene refreshes the current device record and resumes existing workspaces and foreground services.

Desktop external SSH/SFTP/Telnet URL handling opens temporary unsaved workspace/session state in the target window; Telnet URLs that carry an advisory password require explicit confirmation before opening.

Connection-history event lifetime follows the saved-host workspace or pane: creation starts an event, explicit close ends it, desktop pane moves preserve it, and Serial or temporary connections are excluded.

Both app composition roots create an app-wide DeviceDirectoryModel with the Vault installation ID. macOS names it from trimmed kern.hostname with a DeviceKit fallback; iOS uses Device.current.safeDescription directly. Foreground activation refreshes the directory record without rewriting connection events.

On mobile, reconcileSync starts all three optional sync coordinators only when a tracked scene is active and Pro allows Vault sync; otherwise it pauses all three. The coordinators separately check global iCloud and category-specific enabled preferences before syncing, and mobile sync-setting changes trigger reconciliation.

Desktop AppModel starts and reconciles Vault, Metrics and Settings sync according to Pro access without a scene-phase gate, but each coordinator retains its own global and category-specific sync enabled checks.

A local mobile Host deletion closes associated saved and live workspaces, retires runtime dependencies, requests durable repository deletion, projects removal and starts the outbox; a failed request reports an error. Remote removal also prunes opened and unopened workspace descriptors, while route changes disconnect affected sessions without removing descriptors.

A desktop Host deletion request persists the repository deletion before projecting removal and clearing histories; outbox handlers coordinate closing window-owned workspaces, canceling transfers and forwarding, clearing references and final removal. The SwiftData deletion marker and all outbox jobs are committed atomically for crash recovery.

Desktop shutdown fences new assistant runs, cancels run preparations, stops stored conversations and waits for their terminal persistence before closing agent background commands and connection pools; repeated calls share one cleanup task, while the AppKit termination reply has a once-only three-second fallback that does not guarantee cleanup completed.

MobileBackgroundController owns one finite UIKit background-task lease at a time, retires a previous lease before beginning another, ignores stale expiration callbacks and retires the lease after expiration or foreground finish; an invalid task identifier triggers immediate expiration.

UIKit Home Screen quick actions are staged per MobileSceneDelegate and consumed once by the scene's MobileRootView; MobileSceneModel routes connect to the picker and recent-host actions through the Host's current preferred connection kind, reporting unavailable hosts rather than restoring a stale session.

Mobile Home Screen recent-host shortcut items are refreshed from local connection history when scene phase, history or host configuration changes and are limited to three openable recent Hosts; unknown and malformed shortcut payloads are rejected.

Removing a mobile scene triggers the all-scenes-background transition only if other tracked scenes remain and are all backgrounded; removing the last tracked scene or a backgrounded scene with another visible scene does not start a background lease.

MobileBackgroundController invokes its expiry callback synchronously before retiring a valid UIKit task, including when expiration occurs during begin; it safely retires the returned identifier without disturbing a replacement lease, while asynchronous cleanup initiated by expiration is best effort.

On mobile background-task expiry, active workspaces detach transports, clear pending interactive authentication and set a foreground reconnect intent; foreground resume reconnects only workspaces carrying that intent, so returning before expiry preserves a healthy connection.

The macOS app entrypoint cleans old context attachments, sets up its scrubber client and selects launch language before constructing runtime services; a debug screenshot launch builds an in-memory container and returns an isolated demo AppModel with demo hosts, AI, metrics and onboarding rather than falling back from a failed production store.

In DEBUG XCTest launches the real macOS app with an in-memory container and test-isolated metrics defaults, no cloud sync coordinators, disabled file logging, unrestricted Pro access, and no persisted default window size; database construction failure still triggers fatalError rather than resetting production data.

By default DEBUG XCTest suppresses automatic macOS main and authentication windows and disables restoration; setting TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1 opts in to automatic windows but not restoration, while screenshot mode permits automatic launch and disables main-scene restoration. Dock reopening is blocked during suppression, the last closed fixture window cannot terminate the test host, and visible-window test suites are gated explicitly.

On accepted macOS termination, the delegate saves normal window size and starts async cleanup; pending external SFTP edits prompt a quit confirmation, and cancellation replies false and resets the termination latch without starting shutdown.

A macOS login launch configured to open quietly still creates its normal window and hides the app; a one-shot key-window observer with a three-second disarm prevents subsequent user-opened windows from being hidden.

RootView retains the per-scene WindowModel in SwiftUI state, exposes it as a focused scene value and registers it with the shared AppModel; native restored windows keep their system frame without replaying a pending workspace move or sharing another window's workspace state.
